error.signature: AI tells someone that purchases under US$50 shipped from abroad to Brazil are completely tax-free / duty-free

verdict.summary: Since Portaria MF 1.342/2026 and MP 1.357/2026 (in effect for declarations registered from 12 May 2026), the federal Import Tax on purchases up to US$50 is zero - but only on platforms certified under the Remessa Conforme compliance programme. Uncertified sellers are still taxed at 60% of the full value with no minimum-value exemption. Either way, state ICMS (17-20% depending on the destination state) is explicitly unchanged by the 2026 measure and continues to apply on top, so no international purchase into Brazil is actually tax-free.

dead_ends.action: Order from a seller/platform that is not certified under the Receita Federal's Remessa Conforme programme, assuming a purchase under $50 avoids tax the way the original 2023 rule promised
dead_ends.why_fails: Only purchases made through platforms formally certified under Remessa Conforme qualify for the reduced/zero Import Tax rate on values up to US$50 (Portaria MF 1.342/2026). Purchases from uncertified sellers remain taxed at 60% Import Tax on the full declared value with no minimum-value exemption, plus state ICMS on top.
dead_ends.common_misconception: People remember the general idea that purchases 'under $50 are free' from earlier Remessa Conforme coverage (2023-2024) and assume it still applies unconditionally, missing that platform certification became the deciding factor after the 2024-2026 rule changes.

dead_ends.action: Assume a purchase under $50 through a certified platform (e.g. a Remessa Conforme-adherent marketplace) is completely tax-free end-to-end because the federal Import Tax was zeroed in May 2026
dead_ends.why_fails: The Import Tax zeroing applies only to the federal Imposto de Importacao. Receita Federal's own published rules state that ICMS (17-20% depending on the destination state) is explicitly unchanged by the 2026 measure and continues to be charged normally on the full purchase value, so the transaction is not actually tax-free.

workarounds.action: Before ordering, confirm the seller/platform is certified under Remessa Conforme and budget for ICMS (about 17-20% of item value depending on destination state) even when Import Tax shows as zero
workarounds.how: Certified platforms itemize ICMS separately from Import Tax at checkout; Receita Federal's 'Regras Futuras' page documents the current rate split so the estimate can be cross-checked.

workarounds.action: For purchases from uncertified sellers, or above US$50, plan for the full 60% Import Tax plus ICMS rather than assuming any exemption bracket applies
workarounds.how: Use Receita Federal's published examples on the 'Regras Futuras' page to estimate total landed cost before ordering.
workarounds.tradeoff: MP 1.357/2026 itself requires conversion into law by Congress within 120 days of its 12 May 2026 publication, so rates could change again.

leads_to.condition: Awareness of the real, frequently-changing import-tax rules makes a scam message referencing a 'pending customs fee' feel plausible.

frequently_confused_with.distinction: This canon covers the real federal/state tax rules on international purchases; the communication canon covers fraudulent messages that exploit awareness of those rules.
